verses.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָֽטְא֛וּ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî ’a·ḥar had·də·ḇā·rîm hā·’êl·leh ḥā·ṭə·’ū maš·qêh me·leḵ- miṣ·ra·yim wə·hā·’ō·p̄eh la·’ă·ḏō·nê·hem lə·me·leḵ miṣ·rā·yim
verses.literal: Some time later . . . . . . the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master the king of Egypt

verses.original: וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י סָרִיסָ֑יו עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiq·ṣōp̄ par·‘ōh ‘al šə·nê sā·rî·sāw ‘al śar ham·maš·qîm wə·‘al śar hā·’ō·w·p̄îm
verses.literal: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers . . . the chief cupbearer . . . and the chief baker

verses.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖ים אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אָס֥וּר שָֽׁם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yit·tên ’ō·ṯām bə·miš·mar bêṯ śar ha·ṭab·bå̄·ḥīm ’el- bêṯ has·sō·har mə·qō·wm ’ă·šer yō·w·sêp̄ ’ā·sūr šām
verses.literal: and imprisoned them - in the house of the captain of the guard the same prison . . . . . . . . . where Joseph was confined . . .

verses.original: וַ֠יִּפְקֹד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם וַיִּהְי֥וּ יָמִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁמָֽר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yip̄·qōḏ śar haṭ·ṭab·bā·ḥîm ’eṯ- yō·w·sêp̄ ’it·tām way·šā·reṯ ’ō·ṯām way·yih·yū yā·mîm bə·miš·mār
verses.literal: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph and he became their personal attendant After they had been in custody for some time

verses.original: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן חֲלֹמ֑וֹ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·ḥal·mū ḥă·lō·wm šə·nê·hem ’îš ḥă·lō·mōw bə·lay·lāh ’e·ḥāḏ ’îš kə·p̄iṯ·rō·wn ḥă·lō·mōw ham·maš·qeh wə·hā·’ō·p̄eh ’ă·šer lə·me·leḵ miṣ·ra·yim ’ă·šer ’ă·sū·rîm bə·ḇêṯ has·sō·har
verses.literal: both of these men the Egyptian king’s cupbearer and baker who were being held in the prison . . . had a dream . . . . . . on the same . . . night and each dream had its own meaning

verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּ֣רְא אֹתָ֔ם וְהִנָּ֖ם זֹעֲפִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·ḇō ’ă·lê·hem yō·w·sêp̄ bab·bō·qer way·yar ’ō·ṯām wə·hin·nām zō·‘ă·p̄îm
verses.literal: When Joseph came to them in the morning he saw - that they were distraught

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־ סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֛וּעַ פְּנֵיכֶ֥ם רָעִ֖ים הַיּֽוֹם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·’al ’eṯ- sə·rî·sê p̄ar·‘ōh ’ă·šer ’it·tōw ḇə·miš·mar bêṯ ’ă·ḏō·nāw lê·mōr mad·dū·a‘ pə·nê·ḵem rā·‘îm hay·yō·wm
verses.literal: So he asked the officials of Pharaoh who were in custody with him in his master’s . . . house Why are your faces so downcast today

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים סַפְּרוּ־ נָ֖א לִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mə·rū ’ê·lāw ḥă·lō·wm ḥā·lam·nū ū·p̄ō·ṯêr ’ên ’ō·ṯōw way·yō·mer ’ă·lê·hem yō·w·sêp̄ hă·lō·w lê·lō·hîm piṯ·rō·nîm sap·pə·rū- nā lî
verses.literal: We both had dreams . . . they replied . . . but there is no one to interpret them Then Joseph said to them Don’t interpretations belong to God Tell me your dreams . . .

verses.original: וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר־ הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־ חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה־ גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·sap·pêr śar- ham·maš·qîm ’eṯ- ḥă·lō·mōw lə·yō·w·sêp̄ way·yō·mer lōw ba·ḥă·lō·w·mî wə·hin·nêh- ḡe·p̄en lə·p̄ā·nāy
verses.literal: So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream . . . In my dream there was a vine before me

verses.original: וּבַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה שָׂרִיגִ֑ם וְהִ֤יא כְפֹרַ֙חַת֙ עָלְתָ֣ה נִצָּ֔הּ הִבְשִׁ֥ילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶ֖יהָ עֲנָבִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇag·ge·p̄en šə·lō·šāh śā·rî·ḡim wə·hî ḵə·p̄ō·ra·ḥaṯ ‘ā·lə·ṯāh niṣ·ṣāh hiḇ·šî·lū ’aš·kə·lō·ṯe·hā ‘ă·nā·ḇîm
verses.literal: and on the vine were three branches As it budded its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes

verses.original: וְכ֥וֹס פַּרְעֹ֖ה בְּיָדִ֑י וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־ הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־ כּ֣וֹס פַּרְעֹ֔ה וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־ הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־ כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ḵō·ws par·‘ōh bə·yā·ḏî wā·’eq·qaḥ ’eṯ- hā·‘ă·nā·ḇîm wā·’eś·ḥaṭ ’ō·ṯām ’el- kō·ws par·‘ōh wā·’et·tên ’eṯ- hak·kō·ws ‘al- kap̄ par·‘ōh
verses.literal: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand and I took the grapes squeezed them into his cup and placed the cup in his hand

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַשָּׂ֣רִגִ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lōw yō·w·sêp̄ zeh piṯ·rō·nōw šə·lō·šeṯ haś·śā·ri·ḡîm šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm hêm
verses.literal: Joseph replied . . . This is the interpretation The three branches are three days . . .

verses.original: בְּע֣וֹד׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־ רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל־ כַּנֶּ֑ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ כוֹס־ פַּרְעֹה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃
verses.transliteration: bə·‘ō·wḏ šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm yiś·śā p̄ar·‘ōh ’eṯ- rō·še·ḵā wa·hă·šî·ḇə·ḵā ‘al- kan·ne·ḵā wə·nā·ṯa·tā ḵō·ws- par·‘ōh bə·yā·ḏōw kam·miš·pāṭ hā·ri·šō·wn ’ă·šer hā·yî·ṯā maš·qê·hū
verses.literal: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore your position You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand just as you did when you were his cupbearer

verses.original: כִּ֧י אִם־ זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְעָשִֽׂיתָ־ נָּ֥א עִמָּדִ֖י חָ֑סֶד וְהִזְכַּרְתַּ֙נִי֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהוֹצֵאתַ֖נִי מִן־ הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: kî ’im- zə·ḵar·ta·nî ’it·tə·ḵā ka·’ă·šer yî·ṭaḇ lāḵ wə·‘ā·śî·ṯā- nā ‘im·mā·ḏî ḥā·seḏ wə·hiz·kar·ta·nî ’el- par·‘ōh wə·hō·w·ṣê·ṯa·nî min- hab·ba·yiṯ haz·zeh
verses.literal: But . . . when it goes well for you please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh that he might bring me out of this prison

verses.original: כִּֽי־ גֻנֹּ֣ב גֻּנַּ֔בְתִּי מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הָעִבְרִ֑ים וְגַם־ פֹּה֙ לֹא־ עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי מְא֔וּמָה כִּֽי־ שָׂמ֥וּ אֹתִ֖י בַּבּֽוֹר׃
verses.transliteration: kî- ḡun·nōḇ gun·naḇ·tî mê·’e·reṣ hā·‘iḇ·rîm wə·ḡam- pōh lō- ‘ā·śî·ṯî mə·’ū·māh kî- śā·mū ’ō·ṯî bab·bō·wr
verses.literal: For I was kidnapped . . . from the land of the Hebrews and even here I have done nothing . . . for which they should have put me in this dungeon

verses.original: וַיַּ֥רְא שַׂר־ הָאֹפִ֖ים כִּ֣י ט֣וֹב פָּתָ֑ר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אַף־ אֲנִי֙ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה סַלֵּ֥י חֹרִ֖י עַל־ רֹאשִֽׁי׃
verses.transliteration: way·yar śar- hā·’ō·p̄îm kî ṭō·wḇ pā·ṯār way·yō·mer ’el- yō·w·sêp̄ ’ap̄- ’ă·nî ba·ḥă·lō·w·mî wə·hin·nêh šə·lō·šāh sal·lê ḥō·rî ‘al- rō·šî
verses.literal: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable he said to Joseph I too had a dream There were three baskets of white bread on my head

verses.original: וּבַסַּ֣ל הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן מִכֹּ֛ל מַאֲכַ֥ל פַּרְעֹ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹפֶ֑ה וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־ הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃
verses.transliteration: ū·ḇas·sal hā·‘el·yō·wn mik·kōl ma·’ă·ḵal par·‘ōh ma·‘ă·śêh ’ō·p̄eh wə·hā·‘ō·wp̄ ’ō·ḵêl ’ō·ṯām min- has·sal mê·‘al rō·šî
verses.literal: In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh . . . but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head

verses.original: וַיַּ֤עַן יוֹסֵף֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַסַּלִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘an yō·w·sêp̄ way·yō·mer zeh piṯ·rō·nōw šə·lō·šeṯ has·sal·lîm šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm hêm
verses.literal: Joseph . . . replied This is the interpretation The three baskets are three days . . .

verses.original: בְּע֣וֹד׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־ רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל־ עֵ֑ץ וְאָכַ֥ל הָע֛וֹף אֶת־ בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ׃
verses.transliteration: bə·‘ō·wḏ šə·lō·šeṯ yā·mîm yiś·śā p̄ar·‘ōh ’eṯ- rō·šə·ḵā mê·‘ā·le·ḵā wə·ṯā·lāh ’ō·wṯ·ḵā ‘al- ‘êṣ wə·’ā·ḵal hā·‘ō·wp̄ ’eṯ- bə·śā·rə·ḵā mê·‘ā·le·ḵā
verses.literal: Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head . . . and hang you on a tree Then the birds will eat the flesh of your body

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹם הֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־ עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־ רֹ֣אשׁ׀ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־ רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî bay·yō·wm haš·šə·lî·šî yō·wm hul·le·ḏeṯ ’eṯ- par·‘ōh way·ya·‘aś miš·teh lə·ḵāl ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw way·yiś·śā ’eṯ- rōš śar ham·maš·qîm wə·’eṯ- rōš śar hā·’ō·p̄îm bə·ṯō·wḵ ‘ă·ḇā·ḏāw
verses.literal: On the third day which was Pharaoh’s birthday . . . he held a feast for all his officials and in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer - and the chief baker

verses.original: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־ שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל־ מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־ כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yā·šeḇ ’eṯ- śar ham·maš·qîm ‘al- maš·qê·hū way·yit·tên hak·kō·ws ‘al- kap̄ par·‘ōh
verses.literal: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand

verses.original: וְאֵ֛ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים תָּלָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּתַ֛ר לָהֶ֖ם יוֹסֵֽף׃
verses.transliteration: wə·’êṯ śar hā·’ō·p̄îm tā·lāh ka·’ă·šer pā·ṯar lā·hem yō·w·sêp̄
verses.literal: But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker just as Joseph had described to them in his interpretation

verses.original: וְלֹֽא־ זָכַ֧ר שַֽׂר־ הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיִּשְׁכָּחֵֽהוּ׃פ
verses.transliteration: wə·lō- zā·ḵar śar- ham·maš·qîm ’eṯ- yō·w·sêp̄ way·yiš·kā·ḥê·hū
verses.literal: The chief cupbearer however, did not remember Joseph he forgot all about him
